2.content:
METRO is engaging Bristlecone to implement SAP Cloud ALM from January 2026 through October 2026 to support Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management in alignment with the S/4 RISE migration plan, including tenant setup, monitoring and alerting use cases, dashboards, training, and transition support to the METRO team.

- Establish SAP Cloud ALM foundational setup, landscape readiness, and standard change management for the identified METRO systems and integration landscape.
- Configure and validate Technical Monitoring and ChaRM capabilities, including monitoring use cases, alerts, notifications, transport governance, and end-to-end Dev/QA change-cycle testing.
- Deploy the solution in line with the September 2026 go-live and complete hypercare, knowledge transfer, and transition to the METRO team by October 2026.

<IMAGE id="57aeb9cf761c"/>

Key assumptions and any deferred decisions that may affect timeline, scope, or commercial impact are captured in Section 10 and Section 21.

3.1.content:
METRO is planning its transition from SAP Solution Manager 7.2 to SAP Cloud ALM in line with its S/4 RISE migration. The current landscape requires a modern ALM platform that supports standardized change control, technical monitoring, alerting, and release visibility across SAP and integration environments. Solution Manager 7.2 support ends in 2027, which creates a time-bound need to establish a go-forward application lifecycle and operations model on SAP Cloud ALM.

This engagement addresses the need to implement SAP Cloud ALM for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management, including tenant setup, standard change management workflows, monitoring use cases, dashboards, training, and transition support. Key pain points include fragmented monitoring across systems, the need for clearer transport and release governance, and the requirement to align change and monitoring capabilities with the broader S/4 migration timeline. The business driver is to reduce operational overhead, improve traceability and visibility, and enable METRO to adopt SAP’s strategic ALM platform with a controlled deployment by September 2026.

3.2.content:
- Implement SAP Cloud ALM for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management aligned to the S/4 RISE program.
- Establish the SAP Cloud ALM tenant, user management, and required landscape/data flow configuration.
- Configure standard change management workflows, transport routes, and release strategies for Dev, QA, and Production.
- Enable monitoring and alerting for system health, applications, jobs, user performance, and integrations across in-scope landscapes.
- Deliver dashboards for operational monitoring and change management visibility.
- Train METRO users through a train-the-trainer approach and provide transition support during hypercare.
- Achieve deployment in September 2026 and complete knowledge transfer and transition in October 2026.

3.3.content:
In the target state, METRO will use SAP Cloud ALM as the central platform for change and operations governance across the in-scope SAP landscape. The process begins with SAP Cloud ALM subscription, onboarding, and landscape identification, followed by role mapping, monitoring use-case definition, and prerequisite configuration. Change management will then be configured with defined workflows, transport sequencing, and end-to-end testing across Dev and QA before production deployment. In parallel, technical monitoring will be enabled for system health, jobs, user performance, integrations, alerts, and dashboards.

<IMAGE id="57aeb9cf761c"/>

After deployment, Production systems will be incorporated into the change and monitoring model, with issue resolution, document updates, user enablement, and structured transition to the METRO team during hypercare. If a final to-be process diagram is required beyond the implementation timeline view, use <TECH TEAM: confirmed client-facing process flow for Cloud ALM change and monitoring operations>.

4.1.content: Services will be delivered remotely/offshore with coordination through METRO project stakeholders. The implementation scope covers the METRO SAP Cloud ALM tenant and connected landscapes required for the January 2026 to October 2026 delivery window. Country-specific rollout sequencing is not defined in this SOW section; scope is based on the agreed system landscape rather than a country deployment wave.

4.2.content: Process scope includes SAP Cloud ALM standard change management and operational monitoring processes required to support METRO's S/4 RISE migration plan. In-scope processes are change and deployment management, requirements/features/corrections handling, transport sequence mapping across DEV, QA, and PROD, system health monitoring, application monitoring, job monitoring, user performance monitoring for S/4HANA, integration monitoring, notification and alert management, user management within the SAP Cloud ALM tenant, and dashboard enablement for health and change management reporting.

4.3.content:
Technical scope includes SAP Cloud ALM tenant subaccount setup, onboarding, prerequisite configuration readiness, and data flow configuration from connected SAP landscapes into SAP Cloud ALM. Bristlecone will configure standard SAP Cloud ALM capabilities for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management, including transport routes, release strategies, alerting and notifications, monitoring dashboards, production-system mapping in ChaRM workflow, and non-production monitoring use cases through deployment. Technical scope also includes integration enablement for identified SAP systems and integration technologies used by METRO, including S/4HANA Cloud, SAP BTP applications, MII, CPI, Integration Suite, Datasphere, and Ariba, where required for the agreed monitoring and change processes.

<IMAGE id="410e29befe04"/>

- Configuration of standard change management workflow and transport governance setup.
- Configuration of technical monitoring, integration monitoring, dashboards, alerts, and notifications.
- End-to-end test cycle support for Dev and QA ChaRM configuration.
- Train-the-trainer workshop delivery and end-user SOP handover.
- Deployment support for production integration in ChaRM and operations use cases.
- Hypercare, knowledge transfer, document updates, and transition support to the METRO team.

4.5.content: Application scope includes SAP Cloud ALM and the related application functions required for METRO's implementation. In-scope functionalities include SAP Cloud ALM Standard Change Management, Change Request Management, Change & Deployment Management, Requirements/Features/Corrections, SAP Landscape Management, user management in the SAP Cloud ALM tenant, standard health monitoring dashboards, and change management dashboards. Connected application landscape in scope for monitoring and integration enablement includes S/4HANA Cloud, SAP Integration Suite, SAP BTP applications, Datasphere, Ariba, MII, and CPI-supported integration flows relevant to the approved use cases.

5.content:
The proposed solution architecture uses SAP Cloud ALM as the central platform for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management, aligned to METRO’s S/4 RISE migration. SAP Cloud ALM will be configured to support standard change management, transport governance, monitoring use cases, alerting, notifications, dashboards, and transition to the METRO team.

<IMAGE id="499576837090"/>

The deployment model is SAP-hosted SaaS on SAP BTP, with no customer-managed application infrastructure for the ALM platform. The implementation covers onboarding of the SAP Cloud ALM tenant and subaccount, connectivity and data flow from in-scope systems to Cloud ALM, and enablement of monitoring across SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Integration Suite, BTP applications, Datasphere, Ariba, MII, and related landscape components in scope.

Change governance will be based on SAP Cloud ALM standard Change and Deployment Management capabilities. This includes configuration of change workflows, transport route and release strategy setup, mapping of DEV → QA → PROD transport sequencing, production-system mapping in the ChaRM workflow, and role-based authorization aligned to METRO’s user and role matrix. Monitoring governance will include defined use cases, metric thresholds, notification rules, escalation paths, and dashboard visibility for system health, jobs, user performance, and integration exceptions.

The architecture is dependent on finalized landscape identification, confirmed integration technologies, and approved transport governance inputs from METRO. Detailed environment topology, interface connectivity design, and non-functional architecture constraints will be confirmed during the design and onboarding phase with the joint project team.

6.1.content:
The project will be delivered in a phased implementation aligned to METRO’s S/4 RISE migration plan, covering onboarding, design, configuration, testing, deployment, and transition support for SAP Cloud ALM Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management. Delivery will begin with SAP Cloud ALM subscription, technical team onboarding, and landscape identification for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, BTP apps, MII, CPI, and Integration Suite. The design phase will finalize monitoring use cases, metric values, user and role requirements, and the target transport governance model. Realization will configure standard Change Management workflows, transport routes and release strategies, data flow to SAP Cloud ALM, monitoring use cases, dashboards, alerts, and notifications, followed by end-to-end Dev and QA cycle testing. Deployment will add production systems to ChaRM and monitoring scope after landscape go-live readiness is confirmed, then transition knowledge, SOPs, issue resolution, and support responsibilities to the METRO team through hypercare.

16.1.content:
Milestone deliverables shall be governed against the implementation timeline in Section 6, the deliverables defined in Section 9, and the commercials in Section 13. Each milestone shall have a defined due date, responsible owner, and acceptance point before it is treated as complete for invoicing or phase closure.

The milestone baseline for this engagement is: SAP Cloud ALM subscription in January 2026; technical team onboarding in February-April 2026; finalized monitoring use cases and metric values in May 2026; prerequisite configurations readiness in June 2026; Dev and QA ChaRM configuration and end-to-end test cycle in May-September 2026; technical monitoring configuration for non-production systems, alerts, and notifications in May-September 2026; deploy in September 2026; and hypercare transition plan and knowledge transfer in October 2026.

The Milestone Deliverables Matrix shall be maintained as the delivery control point linking phase completion, acceptance evidence, and billing events.

16.2.content:
- Final monitoring use cases and metric thresholds must be frozen by May 2026.
- Customer landscape identification must be completed for S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, and MII before detailed configuration proceeds.
- Integration technology scope must be confirmed for CPI and Integration Suite before integration monitoring configuration is finalized.
- The user and role matrix for SAP Cloud ALM must be approved before tenant access and authorization setup.
- The target transport governance model and transport sequence mapping must be approved before ChaRM realization.
- The RCA process, monitoring schedule, and escalation matrix must be agreed before operational monitoring is handed over.
- Any item not expressly included in the approved scope for Technical Monitoring or Change Request Management shall be treated as out of scope until approved through Section 17.

16.3.content:
- Integration scope shall be limited to the interfaces and technologies identified for this engagement, including S/4, Integration Suite, CPI, BTP, Datasphere, Ariba, S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, and MII, as applicable to the approved use cases.
- Any new integration, monitoring object, landscape, or alerting requirement identified after scope baseline approval shall be assessed for schedule and commercial impact before execution.
- Technical monitoring configuration shall begin only after prerequisite landscape readiness, data flow setup to SAP Cloud ALM, and required access are completed.
- ChaRM configuration shall follow the approved transport governance model, release strategy, and mapped DEV to QA to PROD sequence.
- Production deployment activities shall proceed only after successful go-live readiness of all required landscapes and confirmed cutover readiness for transport migration.
- Custom development outside standard SAP Cloud ALM capabilities is excluded unless separately approved through change control.

16.4.content:
Any change to scope, timeline, deliverables, dependencies, environments, integration coverage, or commercial assumptions shall be managed through the Change Management Process in Section 17. No material change shall be executed on an informal instruction alone.

Change requests shall document the requested change, reason, impact on effort and schedule, dependency impacts, and any effect on acceptance or invoicing. Approved changes shall be reflected in the relevant sections of this SOW, including Sections 6, 9, 13, and 16, before the changed work proceeds. Items arising from deferred decisions, additional landscapes, expanded monitoring coverage, or revised transport governance shall be treated through the same process.

17.content:
Changes to scope, deliverables, timeline, milestones, or commercials will be managed through the following Change Request process. No out-of-scope work will proceed until the applicable Change Request is approved by METRO and Bristlecone and reflected in the governing project documents.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | Either party raises a Change Request when a proposed change affects scope, deliverables, timeline, resources, environments, monitoring use cases, transport governance, or deployment readiness. | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | The Change Request is recorded in the agreed project tracker with a unique reference number and summary of the requested change. | Within 1 business day of receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | Bristlecone assesses impact on scope, effort, schedule, dependencies, testing, cutover, hypercare, and commercials; METRO provides required business and technical inputs. | Within 5 business days of logging, unless otherwise agreed |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | METRO and Bristlecone review the impact assessment and approve, reject, or defer the Change Request through authorized project representatives. | Within 5 business days of impact assessment completion |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | Approved changes that affect contractual scope, milestones, pricing, or term are documented through an amendment, addendum, or other written change instrument under the governing agreement. | Before execution of the approved change |
| 6 | CR closure | After implementation or disposition, the Change Request is updated with final status, effective date, and reference to the related amendment or project-plan update, then closed. | Within 2 business days of implementation or decision |

Changes driven by finalized monitoring use cases, user/role design, customer landscape identification, integration technology confirmation, cutover readiness, or transition planning will follow this process if they affect the agreed baseline. Changes required to support the September 2026 deploy or October 2026 hypercare transition will be prioritized for review against milestone impact. Commercial approval thresholds and signatory authority will follow the governing agreement and METRO project governance.

Upon such notice, the parties will coordinate an orderly wind-down of in-flight activities, including transition of SAP Cloud ALM configuration, project documentation, training materials, and knowledge-transfer items planned through the October 2026 transition period. 19.2.content: Either party may terminate this SOW immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this SOW and fails to cure that breach within the applicable cure period under the governing agreement. Either party may also terminate if the other party becomes insolvent, enters bankruptcy or liquidation proceedings, ceases to do business in the ordinary course, or engages in fraud, willful misconduct, or unlawful activity materially affecting this engagement. If termination for cause occurs due to METRO delay in providing required prerequisites, access, or project alignment, Bristlecone will be entitled to payment for services performed through the termination date.

19.3.content: On termination or expiry of this SOW, Bristlecone will stop work except for activities reasonably required to protect work in progress, support transition, and hand over completed deliverables. Each party will return or securely destroy the other party’s confidential information in accordance with the governing agreement. METRO will pay all undisputed fees for services rendered up to the termination effective date, including completed work related to Cloud ALM onboarding, ChaRM configuration, monitoring setup, dashboards, training, and transition support performed before termination. Termination does not affect accrued payment obligations, confidentiality, intellectual property, limitation of liability, or other provisions that survive under the governing agreement.
